# Typed Jacobi certificate for one terminal reported bit

Date: 2026-09-27. Shared author contribution to activity RA-CAAAC604CB513AEA8BBC1DFC, researcher EM-DIRECT-C6438C. This is author-executed, shared-context evidence, not independent admission. No remote files were changed. The existing target32/vector64 profiles and frozen propagators are unchanged.

## 1. Existing mathematics and the new domain specialization

For positive odd N, write J(a,N) for the Jacobi symbol, with J(a,1)=1. It is a multiplicative character on the units modulo N; it vanishes on nonunits. Its minus-one and two supplements and quadratic reciprocity determine the reduction algorithm. These facts, including the extension to composite odd denominators, are stated in [NIST DLMF 27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9). The factorization definition is mathematical: our algorithm does not receive or compute that factorization.

[Handbook of Applied Cryptography, chapter 2](https://cacr.uwaterloo.ca/hac/about/chap2.pdf), Fact 2.148 and Algorithm 2.149, describes reduction by removing powers of two, applying reciprocity and taking a smaller remainder without factoring N. Table 2.6 and Example 2.152 supply the small known-value fixtures. We implement this established integer algorithm using the already executed BRC division transducer. We do not claim a new Jacobi algorithm.

The new specialization is a compact character certificate for the actual reverse-square Shor work schedule. It replaces an explicit final support-disjointness search by arithmetic in the input labels, on the inputs it certifies. It neither constructs an ideal Shor distribution nor removes the earlier coherent row-query problem.

## 2. Actual arithmetic, algorithm, and replay

`typed_jacobi_trace(a,N)` accepts any non-boolean integer a and positive odd integer N, including 1. It first handles the sign of a using the minus-one supplement. Its initial remainder and every subsequent remainder come from `lazy_modular.Arithmetic.divide`, whose binary long division uses the frozen actual full-adder columns, with complete carry/digit traces. Even factors are removed by right-shift wiring. The low two or three bits select the reciprocity and two-supplement signs; no ordinary `%`, modular `pow`, factorization, or order calculation is used.

An invariant is

    J(original a, original N) = sign * J(x,n).

At an iteration x is positive and n odd. Writing x=2^e u with u odd gives

    J(x,n) = J(2,n)^e * J(u,n)
           = J(2,n)^e * reciprocity_sign * J(n remainder u,u).

When u and n are not coprime, both reciprocal symbols vanish, so the same sign relation remains valid. Otherwise it is the usual reciprocity identity. The new nonnegative numerator is smaller than the new odd denominator u; the Euclidean descent terminates. At termination J(0,n) is 1 for n=1 and 0 otherwise. This proves the output, including zero, negative inputs, and the N=1 convention.

The complete certificate contains every shifted label, sign decision, typed operation, native primitive/source binding, final gcd label, and deterministic work counters. `verify_typed_jacobi` regenerates the complete trace and compares canonical digests. It therefore verifies more than the final sign or a self-reported status. Native kernel invocation counts, which depend on cache warmness, are recorded by the run checker separately from deterministic digit replay counts.

This is an integer certificate observer. It is not a new state propagator, a precision increase, a residual projection, or an ideal-reference dynamics path. Tool coverage was checked at EM d8447e4dc9c6500720c671649798e4ae08df2ae2; see the sibling `latest_frontier/SOURCE_PINS.json`. The route is REUSE_APPLIED for the existing actual arithmetic, and EXTEND for a domain character witness under the existing tool families.

## 3. Final-bit theorem for the actual native instrument

Let N be odd, let a be a unit modulo N, and suppose J(a,N)=-1. Let the t work multipliers, in chronological order, be

    b_i = a^(2^(t-1-i)) modulo N,  0 <= i < t.

The execution starts with work label 1 and the admitted complete internal vector. It uses the existing actual instrument, retaining all signed internal coordinates. At round i and classical history h the full row at a child label z is

    (v_h,z + sigma T_i(h) v_h,P_i^-1 z)/2,

where sigma is +1 or -1, P_i is multiplication by b_i, and T_i(h) is the actual ordered internal feedback isometry. No commuting, ideal-angle or two-coordinate restriction is imposed on T_i(h).

For every i<t-1, b_i is a square in the unit group, hence J(b_i,N)=+1. Starting at J(1,N)=+1, induction on this row formula shows that every reachable nonzero row before the last round has a work label of character +1. Cancellation can remove rows but cannot create a label outside that character class. Feedback changes only internal coordinates.

In the last round P is multiplication by a, so it maps the +1 character class into the disjoint -1 class. Thus for each label z, at least one of

    x = v_h,z,  y = T(h) v_h,P^-1 z

is zero. If M=sum_z ||v_h,z||^2>0, the two raw child masses are

    (sum_z ||x + y||^2)/4 = M/2,
    (sum_z ||x - y||^2)/4 = M/2.

The second equality uses the full isometry norm of T, not a projection. The final reported bit is therefore conditionally fair for every reachable positive-mass earlier history, and hence independent of that earlier history. Zero-mass histories carry no conditional-law claim. The result applies to the actual admitted instrument even when its phases differ from ideal Shor phases.

## 4. Query-free single-walker last step

Assume the existing exact single-walker invariant: conditional on h, latent W has law ||v_h,W||^2/M. Choose an independent fair auxiliary coin C and let Z=W if C=0, or Z=P W if C=1. Then

    Pr(Z=z | h) = (||v_h,z||^2 + ||v_h,P^-1 z||^2)/(2M).

Under the preceding disjointness certificate, the exact joint next-bit/endpoint law is

    Pr(sigma,Z=z | h) = (||v_h,z||^2 + ||v_h,P^-1 z||^2)/(4M).

Consequently an independent fair reported bit after the fair proposal produces exactly that joint law. No final row query or feedback application is needed. The proof preserves the latent endpoint, not merely the bit marginal. The complete history/recipe must still be retained, and any later explicit row reconstruction uses the original oracle and actual words; a sampled latent path is not the full coherent row.

This theorem does not certify an arbitrary injected W or an arbitrary injected intermediate field. Reachability from the original initial state and the latent-law invariant remain required. Runtime wrappers must validate their event/history chain and an unchanged program descriptor, and must fall back to their exact row-query route when the certificate is unavailable.

## 5. Executable certificate boundary

`certify_square_schedule(N,a,t,tables,initial_work_label=1)` accepts an explicit t-entry list/tuple of the existing exact `LazyModularColumns` type. It verifies each distinct complete permutation/inverse certificate, binds every repeated object, requires final multiplier a, and evaluates every adjacent reversed-square relation by fresh typed multiplication and division. It uses neither a full carrier iteration nor `set(table)`. Its return is `CERTIFIED_FINAL_BIT_FAIR` precisely when the valid schedule starts at work 1 and its computed Jacobi value is -1. Otherwise a valid but insufficient witness returns `UNAVAILABLE`, with no inference of unfairness. Malformed inputs, nonunit permutation objects, or false square relations are rejected.

`certify_program_final_bit(program)` binds this witness to the known actual Lazy/SelectedStreamingProgram classes, their canonical initial state, modular descriptor, phase/codec/H4 bindings, and program source hash. It accepts no mid-run state. `verify_program_final_bit(certificate,program)` rebuilds this arithmetic/schedule/descriptor evidence and compares its complete digest. It is deliberately not a second phase-word admission procedure: the existing complete native program admission is a dependency, and its existing source/provenance rules continue to apply. This separation is explicit in the returned certificate. Merely copying `status` out of a JSON object is not authorization to bypass a query.

Neither a certificate nor a Python type alone is a security boundary against arbitrary monkey-patching of trusted code. The scientific contract is an unchanged admitted program, its recorded initial state, and actual transitions. The new character-walker integration is authored separately and should be checked against that contract.

## 6. Costs and scope of improvement

For canonical 0<=a<N and n=bit_length(N), a conservative bound for this simple typed implementation is O(n^3) full-adder digit replays for Jacobi: O(n) Euclidean iterations with at most O(n^2) digit work per division. The reduction by powers of two cannot delay Euclidean termination. For arbitrary larger a, the first division adds polynomial work in bit_length(|a|)+n. We do not claim the optimized O(n^2) arithmetic complexity from HAC for this trace-retaining implementation.

The complete square-schedule witness requires O(t n^3) conservative digit work, including the existing inverse proofs, and polynomial-size retained arithmetic traces. Reusing an already bound schedule can amortize this setup. Hashing and Python allocation are not counted as primitive BRC calls. Native phase compilation/admission is an existing separate dependency and is not hidden in this arithmetic cost. The checker separates actual kernel calls, actual adder-column digit replays, and host bit wiring; the latter is a count of selected wiring operations, not CPU instructions.

There is no |S| or N-entry support enumeration in this character witness. It therefore gives a support-independent, polynomial-bit certificate of one terminal fair bit for the certified inputs, even if the reachable support is large. It does not reduce the number or complexity of the preceding row queries; their full coherent endpoint sums can remain exponential. It also does not certify arbitrary higher-order characters or several terminal bits.

## 7. Bounded execution evidence and counterexamples

`check_typed_jacobi.py` passed 28 known-value cases with complete trace replay, including signs, nonunits, denominator 1, the HAC table/example, and a 66-bit modulus. It passed four square-schedule cases and rejected 17 malformed/tampered controls. A complete actual N=21,a=2,t=4 program descriptor replay passed. The native bank used is the previously frozen direct-word bank, not a newly calculated ideal bank.

Two actual-instrument fixtures check the logical boundary:

* N=21,a=2 has Jacobi -1, but an injected intermediate field with equal e0 rows at work labels {1,2}, at identity-feedback history (0,), yields actual final probabilities 3/4 and 1/4. The reachable-state hypothesis is necessary.
* N=15,a=2 has Jacobi +1 and the new certificate returns UNAVAILABLE. Its original t=2 run nevertheless has a fair last bit at both positive-mass preceding histories. UNAVAILABLE does not mean unfair.

The whole bounded checker recorded 244 native core calls, including bank admission and the native counterexamples. Initial Jacobi generation alone replayed 2,706 full-adder digits and used 263 additional outer label-wiring operations. These are distinct units, not alternative reports of one cost.
